title: Azure Cloud API Error Rate Spike

compliance.assurance_rationale: Saved search evidence for AU-2 when alert outputs are archived.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay or inject sample `azure:monitor:activity` events matching `*` into `index=azure`. Confirm UC-4.4.63 search returns >=1 row and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `azure:monitor:activity` traffic without `*` markers. Confirm the search returns zero rows and alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=azure` sourcetype=`azure:monitor:activity` collected via Splunk cloud TA for Azure; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=azure sourcetype="azure:monitor:activity" errorCode="*"
| table _time operationName caller resourceId resultType
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.63_azure_cloud_api_error_ra_63"
| sort -_time
description: Monitors Azure resources for cloud api error rate spike. This UC monitors `azure:monitor:activity` for azure cloud api error rate spike and surfaces events for SOC triage, change review, and compliance evidence.
value: API error spikes may indicate quota abuse or attack. Detecting azure cloud api error rate spike early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Configure required cloud inputs per provider guide; index=azure sourcetype=azure:monitor:activity.
visualization: Dashboard panel, alert, and weekly compliance report.
knownFalsePositives: Approved change windows; documented automation service principals; sandbox accounts excluded via lookup.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=azure`.
• Install and configure Splunk cloud TA for Azure with the modular input for `azure:monitor:activity`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.4.33.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `operationName` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Configure required cloud inputs per provider guide; index=azure sourcetype=azure:monitor:activity.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="azure:monitor:activity" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="azure:monitor:activity" errorCode="*"
| table _time operationName caller resourceId resultType
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.63_azure_cloud_api_error_ra_63"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `azure:monitor:activity` in `index=azure` to detect azure cloud api error rate spike. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the Azure portal Activity Log blade for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `operationName` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_4_63_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Dashboard panel, alert, and weekly compliance report..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Splunk cloud TA for Azure and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of azure cloud api error rate spike so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
